definitions.explanation: An item of the highest grade or quality. Can refer to physical products or, figuratively, to skills or abilities of outstanding caliber.

examples.japanese: この{革|かわ}は{一級品|いっきゅうひん}だ。
{彼|かれ}の{腕前|うでまえ}は{一級品|いっきゅうひん}だと{評判|ひょうばん}だ。
examples.english: His skill is said to be first-rate.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}では{一級品|いっきゅうひん}の{素材|そざい}だけを{使|つか}った{料理|りょうり}を{提供|ていきょう}している。
examples.english: This restaurant serves dishes made only with first-class ingredients.

notes:
USAGE:
{一級品|いっきゅうひん} literally means "first-grade product" and is used to describe something of the highest quality. It can describe physical goods (leather, fabric, ingredients) or be used figuratively for skills and abilities.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一級品|いっきゅうひん}の{素材|そざい} (first-class materials)
- {一級品|いっきゅうひん}の{味|あじ} (first-class flavor)
- {腕前|うでまえ}は{一級品|いっきゅうひん} (top-notch skill)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{最高級|さいこうきゅう} means "highest grade" and is often used for luxury goods with formal marketing language. {一流|いちりゅう} (first-rate) is broader and describes people, establishments, or quality in general. {一級品|いっきゅうひん} focuses specifically on the item or product itself.
